finding: The case encounter export IS truncated (proven, not suspected)
evidence: Encounters_3 and Encounters_4 each contain exactly 1,048,575 rows (Excel's maximum). They are NOT the same rows: 925,159 keys shared, 123,416 only in file 3, 76,608 only in file 4.
consequence: Two runs of the same query truncated at different points, so both are incomplete. Case encounter counts, last-encounter dates and engagement are all derived from partial data.

finding: 60% of case encounter rows are not clinical visits
evidence: Patient Message 142,956; Clinical Communication 71,235; Orders Only 45,595; Account-less 44,676; Refill 13,587; conversion encounters 38,900. Clinical visit types are 417,586 of 1,048,575 rows (39.8%).
consequence: Encounter density is inflated. Cases show 400.5 rows per patient against 159.5 counting clinical visits only.

finding: The control encounter file has no Encounter Type column
evidence: Controls: Clinic Number, Death Date, Create Date only.
consequence: Cases cannot be filtered to clinical visits unless controls are filtered the same way. Doing it one-sided would recreate the arm asymmetry this analysis exists to remove.

evidence: Engaged on all rows 2,527 of 2,618; on clinical visits only 2,374 of 2,618.
consequence: 153 cases change engagement status depending on which rows count.
